styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, markets and the old centre on foot.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Mercado Central seafood, completos and vineyard day trips.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Andes views, Cerro San Cristóbal and Cajón del Maipo.

stays.why: Walk to the Plaza de Armas, La Moneda and the markets. Busiest and noisiest at night; keep valuables close.
Colourful streets below Cerro San Cristóbal, close to La Chascona and nightlife. Lively, so pick a quiet side street.
Safe, leafy and well connected by Metro Line 1. Good mix of cafés, restaurants and shops.
Modern, calm and close to the Sky Costanera and Parque Arauco. Farther from the old centre; rely on Metro or taxis.

food: Eat seafood at the Mercado Central or Vega Central: try paila marina (shellfish stew) and reineta fish. Prices vary; check the menu before ordering.
Order a completo (hot dog with avocado, tomato and mayo) or an italiano sandwich at a local fuente de soda. Cheap and filling.
Try a pastel de choclo (corn pie) and empanadas de pino. Lunch is the big meal; many places offer a fixed menú at midday.
Coffee culture is strong: order a café or a cortado. For a sweet treat, look for mote con huesillo in summer.
Wine is a highlight. Ask for Chilean Carménère or Sauvignon Blanc by the glass, and consider a day trip to a nearby vineyard.
more_time: Add a day trip to Valparaíso and Viña del Mar: buses leave often from the city, roughly 1.5–2 hours each way. Check schedules on the day.
Swap a city afternoon for Cajón del Maipo in the Andes: book a tour or arrange transport, as public options are limited.
Wine lovers can spend a half-day at a Maipo Valley vineyard. Book ahead; many tastings need a reservation.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the old centre, Cerro San Cristóbal and a market meal, with time for a Valparaíso or vineyard day trip.

month_notes: January: hot and dry, highs near 30°C. Start sightseeing early; many locals are away on holiday.
February: hot and dry, similar to January. Carry water and use sunscreen; afternoons are warm.
March: still warm, highs around 28°C. A good month for walking and vineyard visits.
April: milder, highs near 23°C and cool evenings. Light rain possible; pack a layer.
May: cooler, highs around 19°C. Rain days increase; keep an indoor plan ready.
June: cool and wetter, highs near 16°C. Bring a warm jacket and an umbrella.
July: the coldest month, highs around 15°C and lows near 6°C. Dress in layers.
August: cool and often damp, highs near 16°C. Good for museums and cafés.
September: warming up, highs around 19°C. Rain days still common; check the forecast.
October: pleasant, highs near 22°C. A good balance of mild days and fewer rainy days.
November: warm and mostly dry, highs around 26°C. Great for outdoor sights and day trips.
December: hot and dry, highs near 29°C. Plan shade and water; evenings are comfortable.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate with dry, hot summers and cool, wetter winters. Rain is concentrated from May to September.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Warm, dry days around 26–30°C. Ideal for Cerro San Cristóbal, markets and day trips.

items.title: Wettest months: June to September
items.text: Around 5–6 rain days a month. Carry an umbrella and keep a museum or café backup.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: June to August highs sit near 15–16°C with lows around 6–7°C. Bring a warm jacket.

items.title: Big day-to-night swing
items.text: Even in summer, evenings cool down. A light layer helps after sunset.

items.title: Strong summer sun
items.text: January and February are hot and dry. Use sunscreen, a hat and water.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and sunscreen for summer; layers, a waterproof and sturdy shoes for winter.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; use a bip! card and avoid rush hour.

modes.text: 7 lines and 136 stations, running roughly 06:00–23:00. Pay only with a bip! card; fares about CLP 640–800 by time of day, with free transfers within two hours.
Buses run around the clock on main lines and use the same bip! card. Red line 555 links Pajaritos metro to the airport.
Official taxis are black and yellow. Uber operates but is not officially licensed; agree on the fare or use the meter.
Useful for Andes or vineyard day trips. In the city, traffic and parking make it less practical.
Good in the centre, Bellavista and Providencia. Keep valuables close in busy areas.
Bikes are popular on a growing lane network. Check local rules and lock up securely.
